chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi Khalid said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf in a general manner, so he said: 'Hajj is performed on his behalf from whatever remains of his third.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the boys are made free from the prohibition of hunting (i.e., they enter the state of Ihram without the restriction of hunting) for the Ihram.

key_terms.مُبْهَمًا: In a general or unspecified manner

ai.seo_question: How is a general Hajj bequest fulfilled from the estate, and are children exempt from hunting restrictions during Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a vague bequest for Hajj is fulfilled using the remaining portion of the deceased's one-third estate, ensuring the obligation is met without exceeding the legal limit for bequests. Additionally, it highlights a specific fiqh detail regarding minors, noting that young boys are exempt from the prohibition of hunting (fakh) upon entering Ihram, reflecting the nuanced application of ritual purity and obligations based on age and capacity in Shia jurisprudence.
